root_cause.text: The hash algorithm unregistration loop uses the wrong iterator variable (i instead of j), causing the same algorithm at index i to be unregistered repeatedly instead of iterating through all algorithms from 0 to i.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 93 in eip93-main.c from `crypto_unregister_ahash(&eip93_algs[i]->alg.ahash)` to `crypto_unregister_ahash(&eip93_algs[j]->alg.ahash)`. The function `eip93_unregister_algs(unsigned int i)` receives i as a parameter representing the number of algorithms to unregister, and uses a loop variable j to iterate through indices 0 to i. Using i instead of j in the hash unregistration case causes the same algorithm to be dereferenced and unregistered multiple times in each loop iteration, leading to kernel panic during driver detach.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `eip93_unregister_algs()` function at lines 76-89 contains the vulnerable construct. In the switch statement at line 83, the code uses `eip93_algs[i]->alg.ahash` instead of `eip93_algs[j]->alg.ahash`. The function correctly declares and iterates with variable `j` (line 77: `for (j = 0; j < i; j++)`), but line 83 incorrectly uses `i` instead of `j` in the HASH case: `crypto_unregister_ahash(&eip93_algs[i]->alg.ahash);`. This causes the same algorithm at index `i` to be unregistered repeatedly instead of iterating through all algorithms from 0 to i-1. The SKCIPHER and AEAD cases correctly use `j`, making this inconsistency a clear bug.
